_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Do not report an open queue as `error.Closed`.**

`error.Closed` means that the queue is closed and fully drained. This path also returns it for an open queue after a stale wake.

`src/select.zig:560-618` propagates `getResult` directly. A select caller can therefore treat an open queue as terminal and stop draining future completions. The caller also cannot safely infer that the result is spurious because another task can call `CompletionQueue.close`.

Return a distinct retryable result for the stale-wake case, or make `select` re-register internally after it confirms that the queue is still open. Keep `error.Closed` exclusive to the drained state.

the stale-wake path while the queue remains open. Update the getResult/select
flow, using the symbols getResult and the select handling around its result, to
return a distinct retryable outcome or internally re-register after confirming
the queue is still open, while preserving terminal propagation for genuinely
drained queues.

Agreed on both points — the overload is why the PR is framed as a mitigation rather than the fix, and the multi-closer caller genuinely could not disambiguate. The contract has no retryable value to add without rippling through every select consumer, and select cannot re-register after the win is committed, so this PR now adds the third option: a public `isClosed()`. `error.Closed` with `isClosed() == false` can only be the spurious case, whoever owns the close, so any driver can implement the re-poll safely. `error.Closed` stays truthful for the drained state. The clean fix remains a readiness-verified claim in the wake path — the maintainer's protocol territory, per the PR description.

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Do not treat `isClosed()` as proof that the queue is drained.**

`getResult()` can return `error.Closed` for a stale wake. If another task calls `close()` before this method runs, `isClosed()` returns `true` even though an operation may still be in flight. `close()` leaves such operations running, and `ownerCallback` can later add their results to `completed`. A driver that stops on `true` can leave that completion undrained.

Expose and use one mutex-protected check for `closed && pending.isEmpty() && completed.isEmpty()`, or preserve the drained-versus-spurious classification from `getResult()`. `isClosed()` alone does not provide the terminal-state guarantee described here.

✅ Addressed in commit 646a0b4

`@dimenus`, `isClosed() == false` does identify a spurious result safely. The converse does not hold.

A stale wake can reach `getResult()` after another task calls `close()` while operations remain in `pending`. `getResult()` then returns `error.Closed` because `completed` is empty. A subsequent `isClosed()` returns `true`, but the queue was not drained. A driver that stops on that result leaves the pending operations undrained.

`getResult()` must check the drained condition under the same mutex acquisition that pops `completed`, or `select` must retry the non-drained case internally. `isClosed()` is useful for diagnostics and caller policy, but it cannot make `error.Closed` exclusive to the terminal state.

<sub>You are interacting with an AI system.</sub>

<!-- This is an auto-generated reply by CodeRabbit -->

You're right, and the second finding caught a real hole in my accessor: isClosed() blesses a stop in exactly the closed-but-not-drained case, where ownerCallback still delivers in-flight completions and stopping leaks them. Replaced with isDrained() — one mutex-protected check of closed-and-pending-empty-and-completed-empty. That unifies the driver rule for every case this thread raised: error.Closed with isDrained() == false always means keep driving (stale wake on an open queue, or a close with work still in flight), and true is the terminal state the error describes. The races around the check run in the safe direction: a completion landing after the empty pop reads not-drained and the next poll takes it. The contract itself still cannot express a retry, and select cannot re-register a committed win without protocol surgery — that remains the real fix, deferred to the maintainer per the PR description.

Addressed together with the sibling thread: isClosed() is gone, replaced by isDrained() with exactly the mutex-protected closed-and-pending-empty-and-completed-empty check this finding asks for. A driver stops only on that predicate, so the closed-with-inflight case keeps draining and nothing leaks.

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Update the module-level `select` contract.**

The documentation at Lines 52-57 says a `select` result matches `wait` except for cancellation. This change also allows `select` to return `error.Closed` for a stale wake while the queue is open. A driver following the module-level documentation can stop and leave later completions undrained. Document the `isDrained()` check and the required re-poll when it returns `false`.

✅ Addressed in commit 6bba7be

`@dimenus`, confirmed. `isDrained()` checks `closed`, `pending`, and `completed` under one mutex acquisition.

After `getResult()` returns `error.Closed`, a driver continues when `isDrained()` is `false`. It stops only when `isDrained()` is `true`. This covers both stale wakes and closed queues with operations still in flight.

The race described is safe. A completion that arrives after `getResult()` finds no node makes `isDrained()` return `false`, and the next poll can take that completion.

_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Clean up the queue before returning `error.Spurious`.**

Line 96 bypasses the teardown at Lines 127-132. Pending operations can still call back through stack-backed `cq`, `recv_op`, or `t1` after `driver` unwinds. This can convert a detected spurious win into a crash or hang.

Add an `errdefer` after Line 75 that closes and cancels the queue before the local operations and file descriptors leave scope.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         var cq = zio.CompletionQueue.init();
+        errdefer {
+            cq.close();
+            cq.cancelAll(.discard);
+        }
         var recv_buf: [64]u8 = undefined;
```
</details>
